analysis.title: [UBS Private Markets Roundup] Week of 9 Nov
key_insights: OpenAI generated $10B of revenue in the September quarter, nearly 50% more than the prior quarter and almost three times the year-ago level.

OpenAI reportedly completed an initial $11B financing at a $1.25T valuation, below earlier reported ambitions and short of the full amount originally sought. UBS reads this as strong investor appetite with some selectiveness on price.

Other frontier AI financings: Thinking Machines Lab reportedly nearing a $5B raise at a $40B pre-money valuation, Mercor raised $750M at a $20B valuation, and TSMC approved a potential investment of up to $500M in OpenAI preferred shares.
UBS says the debate remains open on how much return the capital poured into compute, infrastructure, talent and training can ultimately generate, since the cost of staying competitive keeps rising.
Power is a constraint on data-center build-out. Norway's Statnett paused new data-center grid reservations after reaching 4.2GW reserved, with 9.1GW in the connection queue and 18GW of inquiries.
Google acquired Crusoe's Wyoming data-center site and plans to invest $17B in the project after cost and timing concerns emerged around the development.

UBS's Karl Keirstead spoke with more than 15 data-center industry contacts after the US midterms. They agreed permitting and community opposition have become greater risks, but the checks were more sanguine on what follows.

Tighter approvals should fall disproportionately on new developments and 2028-plus capacity, while projects already permitted or under construction appear better protected. Louisiana, West Virginia and Missouri were cited as potential beneficiaries if developers meet more resistance elsewhere.

Data-center financing is getting more selective, with lenders wanting investment-grade offtakers, stronger contracts and execution confidence, but the market remains open. ING was reportedly marketing roughly $500M of data-center loans last week.

Permitting, labor, transformers, breakers and utility coordination can delay go-live dates, and one UBS check suggested six months can materially change a project's IRR. One estimate puts roughly two-thirds of current US projects as having met some opposition.

UBS expects the build-out to continue but to favor companies that already have customers, capital, relationships and the ability to deliver, which favors larger hyperscalers over speculative projects.

Applied AI startups are raising in narrow niches. Kalepa raised $75M at a $470M valuation after reportedly quadrupling usage of its insurance underwriting platform, and Otter is expanding beyond transcription into meeting preparation and coaching.

Primordial Labs raised an $18M Series A for Anura, a natural-language command interface for crewed and uncrewed military platforms. Alta Ares won six of 16 lots in a NATO counter-drone framework and targets over 1,000 interceptors a month by 2027, though framework selection does not guarantee purchase volumes.
PitchBook identified $2.1B of investment across 55 physical-AI data deals, with firms collecting human demonstrations and real-world data to train robots.

Raahul Ramakrishnan, newly leading UBS Healthcare Private Markets Research, estimates more than $130B has gone into US and Canadian private healthcare companies in 2026 YTD. His initiation maps $61.8B across 1,107 Series A-C financings since 2024 into 20 themes.
UBS calculates an implied $500-550B 2030 TAM for private healthcare, using assumptions on target returns, valuation multiples and private-market share capture.

Segment split: Pharma and biotech $30.2B across 367 financings with a $200-225B 2030 TAM, medtech $11.8B across 317, HealthTech and Services $14.6B across 426 with a $125-150B TAM, and Life Sciences Tools and Diagnostics $5.1B against a $50-75B TAM.

UBS flags that where the most capital has gone and where the best risk-adjusted opportunity sits may differ. Open questions include whether AI repeatedly produces better medicines and whether healthcare automation removes work or just shifts it.
Oura announced a $625M acquisition of Counsel Health, adding AI medical guidance and physician access to Oura's biometric data. Oura reported about $1.75B of FY2026 revenue, up 92% YoY.

UBS secondary privates desk indications: Bytedance two sided. OpenAI, Stripe, Harvey and Supabase better to buy. Discord and WHOOP better for sale. Ripple two ways with buy skew. Tether, Perplexity, Helion better to sell. Fanatics and ShieldAI have sellers in the market.
UBS research roundup includes a Private Credit podcast noting rates continue to rise and spreads are finally responding.

UBS Semis compendium profiles 105 private semiconductor companies, 79 of them new, across AI inference, networking, edge and advanced packaging. Recent funding at Cerebras, Groq, SambaNova and Etched points to continued conviction in the AI infrastructure build-out.
UBS Internet spotlight estimates the global autonomous logistics and warehousing robotics market at $34.5B in 2035, a 10-year CAGR of 22.7% per third-party data.

UBS's agentic commerce discussion suggested card networks remain well positioned for consumer transactions given dispute rights, while stablecoins and programmable rails may gain traction in settlement, treasury, cross-border and B2B use cases.

Private biotech note cites recent rounds of $311m for Enveda, $220m for CellCentric and $125m for Ray Therapeutics. The US Biotech compendium notes pharma faces more than $400bn of loss-of-exclusivity exposure over the coming decade.
Private trucking brokers remain constructive on the truckload pricing cycle, supported by seasonal demand and continued pressure on industry capacity.

Private company funding data points in the roundup include Fireworks AI ($1.5bn Series D at $17.5bn), Tempo ($500m Series A at $5bn), Glean ($150m Series F at $7.2bn), Multiverse Computing ($570m Series C), Rogo (about $190m at about $2bn) and SpotOn ($300m Series F at about $3.6bn).

sector_views.rationale: UBS industry checks are less bearish than headlines, with the build-out continuing but favoring players with power, capital, customers and credibility. Permitting and community opposition are rising risks for new developments and 2028-plus capacity.

UBS sees an implied $500-550B 2030 TAM and heavy funding, but says the harder questions begin after the technology works, including who owns the workflow and how much of the economics the private company retains.

Oura (private) reported approximately $1.75B of FY2026 revenue, up 92% YoY.

crypto_views: UBS secondary desk indicates Ripple is two ways with a buy skew and Tether is better to sell.

UBS discussion on agentic commerce suggested stablecoins and programmable payment rails may gain traction in settlement, treasury, cross-border and high-frequency B2B use cases as agentic commerce scales.

Allium provides blockchain data infrastructure across 150+ chains and raised a $40m Series B led by Amplify Partners in June 2026. UBS frames it as picks-and-shovels exposure to institutional onchain finance.

Rimark's Solstice Protocol targets bank-issued tokenized deposits and real-time settlement. More than 60 banks were reported backing the initial DTX pilot with the Independent Bankers Association of Texas.
UBS hosted the Solana Foundation and Zero Hash in its audio interview series, and covered Tempo, a payments blockchain that reportedly raised a $500m Series A at a $5bn valuation.
risk_factors: Frontier AI valuations and funding targets may not be fully met even with strong growth, as shown by OpenAI's $11B raise at $1.25T falling short of earlier ambitions.
Rising compute, infrastructure, talent and training costs keep the return on AI capital an open question.
Data-center permitting, community opposition, power scarcity, labor, transformer and breaker supply and utility coordination can delay projects. A six-month delay can materially change IRR.
Data-center lenders increasingly require investment-grade offtakers and stronger contracts, which disadvantages speculative projects.
Healthcare technology funding may not translate into better outcomes or economics worth owning, and capital allocation may diverge from the best risk-adjusted opportunity.
Framework selection in NATO counter-drone procurement does not guarantee purchase volumes.
